alchemists.name: Jabir ibn Hayyan
alchemists.context_snippet: Foundational Islamic alchemist; pioneered systematic distillation and sublimation operations

alchemists.name: Zosimos
alchemists.context_snippet: Late Antique Greco-Egyptian alchemist; author of the oldest known alchemical treatises

alchemists.name: Mary the Prophetess
alchemists.context_snippet: One of the earliest known alchemists; credited with inventing the bain-marie and other lab apparatus

alchemists.name: Hermes Trismegistus
alchemists.context_snippet: Legendary founder of alchemy and Hermeticism; attributed to works compiled in Late Antiquity

alchemists.name: Al-Razi
alchemists.context_snippet: Persian physician and alchemist; known for medical and chemical treatises

alchemists.name: Avicenna
alchemists.context_snippet: Influential Persian physician and philosopher; works shaped medieval alchemy and medicine

alchemists.name: Albertus Magnus
alchemists.context_snippet: Dominican friar; encyclopedic writer on natural philosophy and alchemy; teacher of Thomas Aquinas

alchemists.name: Thomas Aquinas
alchemists.context_snippet: Dominican friar and scholastic theologian; author of Aurora Consurgens (alchemical treatise)

alchemists.name: Roger Bacon
alchemists.context_snippet: Franciscan friar and natural philosopher; wrote on alchemy and experimental method

alchemists.name: Arnaud de Villanova
alchemists.context_snippet: Catalan physician and alchemist; wrote extensively on alchemy and medicine; subject of Rosarium Philosophorum

alchemists.name: Dante Alighieri
alchemists.context_snippet: Italian poet and intellectual; influenced by alchemical symbolism and medieval philosophy

alchemists.name: Nicholas Flamel
alchemists.context_snippet: Legendary Parisian alchemist; popularized transmutational claims and alchemical symbolism in medieval Europe

alchemists.name: Johann Trithemius
alchemists.context_snippet: Benedictine abbot; wrote on occult philosophy and alchemy; teacher of Paracelsus

alchemists.name: Paracelsus
alternate_names: Theophrastus Philippus Aureolus Bombastus von Hohenheim
alchemists.context_snippet: Swiss physician and alchemist; revolutionized alchemical theory by linking it to medicine and metallurgy

alchemists.name: John Dee
alchemists.context_snippet: English mathematician and occultist; extensive alchemical and Hermetic library; advisor to Elizabeth I

alchemists.name: George Ripley
alchemists.context_snippet: English Augustinian canon and alchemist; author of the Compound of Alchymy

alchemists.name: Christian Rosencreutz
alchemists.context_snippet: Legendary founder of the Rosicrucian order; subject of Chemical Wedding and other esoteric texts

alchemists.name: Robert Boyle
alchemists.context_snippet: Anglo-Irish natural philosopher; early modern chemist; combined alchemical and experimental methods

alchemists.name: Isaac Newton
alchemists.context_snippet: English physicist and mathematician; conducted extensive alchemical and transmutational experiments

alchemists.name: George Starkey
alchemists.context_snippet: 17th-century alchemist; published under pseudonym Eirenaeus Philalethes; known for practical alchemy

alchemists.name: Geoffrey Chaucer
alchemists.context_snippet: English poet; incorporated alchemical references and imagery in Canterbury Tales and other works

scholars.name: William R. Newman
scholars.scholarly_focus: Operational chemistry, transmutation theory, Jabir ibn Hayyan, medieval alchemy, proto-chemistry
scholars.historiographical_position: Argues that medieval alchemists pursued genuine chemical operations through rigorous empirical methods
scholars.context_snippet: Newman reframes medieval alchemy as proto-chemistry with genuine experimental rigor

scholars.name: Michela Pereira
key_works: The Alchemical Corpus Attributed to Ray Lull
scholars.scholarly_focus: Medieval alchemy, Catalan alchemical tradition, Ray Lull
scholars.historiographical_position: Emphasizes the role of Mediterranean and Catalan alchemy in medieval European intellectual networks
scholars.context_snippet: Pereira documents the Catalan alchemical tradition and Ray Lull's central role

scholars.name: Lawrence Principe
scholars.scholarly_focus: Practical alchemy, Robert Boyle, Isaac Newton, early modern alchemy, laboratory reconstruction
scholars.historiographical_position: Reconstructs alchemical practice through laboratory work and empirical investigation
scholars.context_snippet: Principe reconstructs historical alchemical operations through modern laboratory experimentation

scholars.name: Wouter J. Hanegraaff
key_works: Dictionary of Gnosis and Western Esotericism
scholars.historiographical_position: Develops rigorous frameworks for understanding esotericism and alchemy in intellectual history
scholars.context_snippet: Hanegraaff establishes the Actor/Analyst distinction central to alchemical historiography

scholars.name: Garth Fowden
scholars.scholarly_focus: Late Antique alchemy, Zosimos, Byzantine alchemy, Hermeticism, Neoplatonism
scholars.historiographical_position: Traces the Late Antique roots of alchemy and its synthesis with Neoplatonic philosophy
scholars.context_snippet: Fowden traces Hermetic and alchemical traditions to Late Antique Egypt and Neoplatonic philosophy

scholars.name: Pamela Smith
scholars.scholarly_focus: Early modern alchemy, craft knowledge, transmutation, patronage, practical chemistry
scholars.historiographical_position: Emphasizes the economic, social, and material dimensions of early modern alchemical practice
scholars.context_snippet: Smith situates alchemy within early modern economies of knowledge and craft production

scholars.name: Eric John Holmyard
scholars.scholarly_focus: Alchemy history, overview, medieval alchemy, classical alchemy
scholars.historiographical_position: Comprehensive historical survey emphasizing the evolution from ancient chemistry through early modern period
scholars.context_snippet: Holmyard provides the foundational chronological survey of alchemy from antiquity to early modern

scholars.name: Adam McLean
key_works: The Alchemical Emblem in the Western Tradition
A Commentary on the Mutus Liber
scholars.scholarly_focus: Alchemical symbolism, emblems, visual alchemy, esoteric philosophy
scholars.historiographical_position: Explores alchemical texts through symbolic, emblematic, and mystical interpretations
scholars.context_snippet: McLean offers detailed symbolic commentary on alchemical emblems and visual traditions

scholars.name: Lyndy Abraham
scholars.scholarly_focus: Alchemical imagery, symbolism, psychological interpretation, gender in alchemy
scholars.historiographical_position: Analyzes alchemical symbols through literary, psychoanalytic, and gender-critical perspectives
scholars.context_snippet: Abraham catalogs alchemical imagery with attention to psychological and gender dimensions

texts.title: Summa Perfectionis
texts.date_or_period: c. 1300 (Arabic original c. 9th century, Latin translation 12th-13th century)
texts.significance_described: The most widely cited authority in medieval and Renaissance European alchemy; systematizes distillation, sublimation, and transmutational theory

texts.title: Rosarium Philosophorum
texts.author_or_tradition: Anonymous/Compiled (attributed variously to Arnaud de Villanova, Islamic sources)
texts.significance_described: Foundational Renaissance alchemical compilation; includes 20 emblematic woodcuts; synthesizes medieval and Islamic alchemy

texts.title: Emerald Tablet
texts.significance_described: Foundational Hermetic text; inscribed with the principle of sympathy and correspondence (As above, so below)

texts.title: Book of Lambspring
texts.significance_described: Emblematic alchemical text with poetic commentary on the creation of the philosopher's stone

texts.title: Mutus Liber
texts.significance_described: Completely nonverbal alchemical treatise consisting of 15 emblems with 1 brief Latin inscription; revolutionary in form

texts.title: Chemical Wedding
texts.significance_described: Foundational Rosicrucian text; allegorical account of a mystical marriage combining alchemy, Hermeticism, and Christian symbolism

texts.title: Atalanta Fugiens
texts.significance_described: Emblematic alchemical treatise with 50 engravings; combines emblems, musical fugas, and epigrams

texts.title: Turba Philosophorum
texts.date_or_period: c. 12th century (Latin translation from 9th-century Arabic original)
texts.significance_described: Medieval dialogue-form compilation of earlier alchemical teachings; widely cited in European alchemy

texts.title: Aurora Consurgens
texts.significance_described: Scholastic alchemical commentary synthesizing Aristotelian philosophy with alchemical operations

texts.title: Splendor Solis
texts.significance_described: Emblematic alchemical treatise with 22 hand-colored engravings depicting the stages of the Great Work

texts.title: Medea
texts.significance_described: Alchemical commentary disguised as commentary on Seneca's classical drama; uses theatrical narrative for alchemical allegory
